If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{1}{4} & f'(1) & 1 \\ \alpha^{2} & 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \mathrm{adj}(\mathrm{adj}\,A)$ be such that $|B| = 81$, then $\alpha^{2}$ is equal to :

$\left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{4}{7}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3^{2}} + \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{4}{7} + \frac{4^{2}}{7^{2}}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3^{3}} + \frac{1}{3^{2}} \times \frac{4}{7} + \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{4^{2}}{7^{2}} + \frac{4^{3}}{7^{3}}\right) + \ldots$ upto infinite terms, is equal to :
questions.solution:
$$\left(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{4}{7}\right) + \left(\frac{1}{3^{2}} + \frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{4}{7} + \frac{4^{2}}{7^{2}}\right) + \ldots\ldots \infty$$
$$(a + b) + \left(a^{2} + ab + b^{2}\right) + \left(a^{3} + a^{2}b + ab^{2} + b^{3}\right) + \ldots \infty$$
$$\frac{\left(a^{2} - b^{2}\right) + \left(a^{3} - b^{3}\right) + \left(a^{4} - b^{4}\right) + \ldots + \infty}{a - b}$$
$$\frac{\left(\frac{a^{2}}{1 - a}\right) - \left(\frac{b^{2}}{1 - b}\right)}{a - b}$$
$$\frac{a^{2}(1 - b) - b^{2}(1 - a)}{(a - b)(1 - a)(1 - b)}$$
$$\frac{a + b - ab}{1 - a - b + ab}$$
$$\frac{\frac{1}{3} + \frac{4}{7} - \frac{4}{21}}{1 - \frac{1}{3} - \frac{4}{7} + \frac{4}{21}} = \frac{5}{2}$$

Let the angles made with the positive x-axis by two straight lines drawn from the point $P(2, 3)$ and meeting the line $x + y = 6$ at a distance $\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$ from the point P be $\theta_{1}$ and $\theta_{2}$. Then the value of $(\theta_{1} + \theta_{2})$ is :
questions.solution:
(Figure: line $x + y = 6$ and a line from $P(2, 3)$ meeting it at A, with $PA = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}$.)
$$A\left(2 \pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\cos\theta, 3 \pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\sin\theta\right)$$
$x + y = 6$
$$5 \pm \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}(\cos\theta + \sin\theta) = 6$$
$$\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \pm\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}$$
$$1 + \sin 2\theta = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$\frac{2\tan\theta}{1 + \tan^{2}\theta} = \frac{1}{2}$$
$\tan^{2}\theta - 4\tan\theta + 1 = 0$ (roots $\tan\theta_{1}$, $\tan\theta_{2}$)
$$\tan\left(\theta_{1} + \theta_{2}\right) = \frac{\tan\theta_{1} + \tan\theta_{2}}{1 - \tan\theta_{1} \cdot \tan\theta_{2}}$$
$$\theta_{1} + \theta_{2} = \tan^{-1}(\infty) = \frac{\pi}{2}$$

questions.stem:
Consider the following three statements for the function $f : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x) = |\log_{e} x| - |x - 1|$
(I) $f$ is differentiable at all $x > 0$.
(II) $f$ is increasing in $(0, 1)$.
(III) $f$ is decreasing in $(1, \infty)$ then :
questions.solution:
$f : (0, \infty) \to \mathbb{R}$
$f(x) = |\ln x| - |x - 1|$
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} -\ln x + x - 1 & 0 < x < 1 \\ \ln x - x + 1 & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$$
$$f'(x) = \begin{cases} 1 - \frac{1}{x} & 0 < x < 1 \\ \frac{1}{x} - 1 & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$$
$f'\left(1^{+}\right) = f'\left(1^{-}\right) = 0$ Diff at all $x > 0$
in $x \in (0, 1) \Rightarrow f'(x) = 1 - \frac{1}{x}$
$f'(x) < 0 \Rightarrow f(x)$ is decreasing
in $x \in (1, \infty) \Rightarrow f'(x) = \frac{1}{x} - 1$
$f'(x) < 0 \Rightarrow f(x)$ is decreasing

Let $[t]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. If the function
$$f(x) = \begin{cases} b^{2}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\left[\frac{\pi}{2}(\cos x + \sin x)\cos x\right]\right), & x < 0 \\ \frac{\sin x - \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x}{x^{3}}, & x > 0 \\ a, & x = 0 \end{cases}$$
is continuous at $x = 0$, then $a^{2} + b^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
for cont. at $x = 0$
$f(0) = f(0^{+}) = f(0^{-})$
$$a = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{2\sin x - \sin 2x}{2x^{3}} = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} b^{2}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\left[\frac{\pi}{2}(\sin x + \cos x)\cos x\right]\right)$$
$$a = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{2\left(x - \frac{x^{3}}{3!}\right) - \left(2x - \frac{8x^{3}}{3!}\right)}{2x^{3}} = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} b^{2}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$$
$$a = \frac{1}{2} = b^{2}$$
$$a^{2} + b^{2} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Let $f(\alpha)$ denote the area of the region in the first quadrant bounded by $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y^{2} = x$ and $y = |\alpha x - 5| - |1 - \alpha x| + \alpha x^{2}$. Then $(f(0) + f(1))$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$x = 0, x = 1, y^{2} = x$
$f(0) \Rightarrow \alpha = 0$
$y = 4$
$$f(0) = 4 - \int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x}\,dx = 4 - \frac{2}{3}\left(x^{3/2}\right)_{0}^{1} = \frac{10}{3}$$
$f(1) \Rightarrow \alpha = 1$
(Figure: shaded region between $y^{2} = x$ and $y = 4$ for $0 \le x \le 1$.)
$y = 4 + x^{2}$
(Figure: shaded region between $y^{2} = x$ and $y = 4 + x^{2}$ for $0 \le x \le 1$.)
$$f(1) = \int_{0}^{1}\left(4 + x^{2} - \sqrt{x}\right)dx$$
$$f(1) = \left(4x + \frac{x^{3}}{3} - \frac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right)_{0}^{1}$$
$$f(1) = 4 + \frac{1}{3} - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{11}{3}$$
$$f(0) + f(1) = \frac{21}{3} = 7$$

questions.solution:
$\tan(x + 100) = \tan(x + 50)\tan x \tan(x - 50)$
$$\frac{\sin\left(x + 100^\circ\right)\cos\left(x - 50^\circ\right)}{\cos\left(x + 100^\circ\right)\sin\left(x - 50^\circ\right)} = \frac{\sin\left(x + 50^\circ\right)\sin x}{\cos\left(x + 50^\circ\right)\cos x}$$
Apply C & D
$$\frac{\sin\left(2x + 50^\circ\right)}{\sin\left(150^\circ\right)} = \frac{\cos\left(50^\circ\right)}{-\cos\left(2x + 50^\circ\right)}$$
$\sin\left(4x + 100^\circ\right) = -\cos\left(50^\circ\right)$
$\sin\left(4x + 100^\circ\right) = \sin\left(-40^\circ\right)$
$4x + 100 = n\pi - (-1)^{n}\left(40^\circ\right)$
$x = 30^\circ, 55^\circ, 120^\circ, 145^\circ$

Let S be a set of 5 elements and $P(S)$ denote the power set of S. Let E be an event of choosing an ordered pair $(A, B)$ from the set $P(S) \times P(S)$ such that $A \cap B = \varnothing$. If the probability of the event E is $\frac{3^{p}}{2^{q}}$, where $p, q \in \mathbb{N}$, then $p + q$ is equal to ________.
If $f(x)$ satisfies the relation $f(x) = e^{x} + \int_{0}^{1}\left(y + xe^{x}\right)f(y)\,dy$, then $e + f(0)$ is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
$$f(x) = e^{x} + \int_{0}^{1}\left(y + xe^{x}\right)f(y)\,dy$$
$$f(x) = e^{x} + xe^{x}\int_{0}^{1}f(y)\,dy + \int_{0}^{1}yf(y)\,dy$$
$f(x) = e^{x} + \lambda xe^{x} + \mu$
$$\lambda = \int_{0}^{1}f(y)\,dy$$
$$\lambda = \int_{0}^{1}\left(e^{y} + \lambda ye^{y} + \mu\right)dy$$
$$\lambda = \left(e^{y} + \lambda\left(ye^{y} - e^{y}\right) + \mu y\right)_{0}^{1}$$
$\lambda = (e + \mu) - (1 - \lambda)$
$\mu = 1 - e$
$f(0) = e^{0} + 0 + 1 - e$
$f(0) = 2 - e$
$f(0) + e = 2$
